Have questions? We’ve got them covered.

#### Weight Watchers Med+ helps make accessing a weight-loss medication convenient   and easy, if you qualify, through a brand you know and trust.

### What are weight-loss meds?

Weight loss meds, including GLP-1s like Wegovy **®** or Zepbound **®**, can help you feel fuller longer, and reduce appetite.

### How much weight can I expect to lose?

Our Med+ members lose 21% of their body weight in 12 months on average with a GLP-1 medication.\*

### What meds are available?

We only prescribe FDA-approved medications, available in both injection and injection-free options.

### Will insurance cover meds?

Many meds are covered by insurance, and we also offer cash-pay options. Your insurance coordinator will make the calls to help maximize your coverage–plus manage pre-authorizations and refills.

\*In a study of 3,250 WW Clinic patients, patients that were prescribed a GLP-1 lost on average 21% of their body weight at 12 months.

[See if you qualify](https://www.weightwatchers.com/us/personalassessment/clinical-v4/main-goal)

Members lose 29% more weight^

#### GLP-1s support your biology. Weight Watchers supports healthy habits. Weight Watchers gives you access to both: Med+ members who engaged regularly with the GLP-1 Success Program **lost 29.1% more body weight**, on average, in 12 months than those who did not engage in behavioral support.^

^Based on an internal analysis of 3,325 members who requested at least 1 GLP-1 medication refill through Weight Watchers Med+ and self-reported both a starting weight and weight at week 52. On average, members who logged in to the GLP-1 Success Program at least 4 days each week (n=376) lost 22.20% body weight, and members who never logged in to the app (n=2,949) lost 17.20% body weight in 52 weeks. Not a randomized, controlled clinical trial. Self-reported outcomes have not been independently verified. Individual results may vary.

### **What are GLP-1s?**

- GLP-1 receptor agonists mimic naturally-occurring hormones that signal fullness to the brain and slow emptying in the gut.


- GLP-1 prescription meds mimic these hormones to support genetic, biological and environmental factors that may make weight loss more difficult.


- Reduced food noise and cravings, plus feeling fuller longer, results in lifestyle changes that lead to more effective weight loss.


### **Are they safe?**

- GLP-1s are FDA-approved and clinically proven medications.


- The most common side effects are nausea, constipation, or other gastrointestinal discomfort.


- Your Care Team will advise you on the best ways to minimize side effects.

Frequently asked questions

What medications do you prescribe?

The exact medication that your Clinician will prescribe depends on your medical history, biology, and insurance coverage. When appropriate, your Clinician may prescribe GLP-1 medications, including semaglutide (brand name Wegovy), liraglutide (brand name Saxenda), or tirzepatide (brand name Zepbound). When appropriate, your clinician may prescribe other weight-loss drugs with which other members have found success such as Metformin and combination Naltrexone and Bupropion. If your treatment plan isn’t working for you, talk to your Weight Watchers Med+ Care Team about adjustments or alternative plans.

Please note, some GLP-1 medications are experiencing intermittent nationwide shortages. See which medications are affected on the FDA shortage database.

Is medication included in my membership fee?

It depends on your treatment plan. For GLP-1 medications, your medications are not included, but your Care Team will work with you to get your medication covered by insurance. If insurance covers your medication, you may still be responsible for a copay.

For non-GLP-1 medications, your medications are included in the cost of membership when you choose our mail-order pharmacy partner, Carepoint.

Carepoint's address is 9 Commerce Dr, Schaumburg, IL 60173.

What are the typical results with GLP-1s?

Results depend on which medication you’re prescribed and your medical history. Typically, patients on a GLP-1 medication will lose 10-20% of their body weight. Learn [how GLP-1s for weight loss really work](https://www.weightwatchers.com/us/blog/weight-loss/glp-1-for-weight-loss).

Learn more in [this study](https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(22)02403-5/abstract) summarizing the efficacy of various weight management treatments.

Are there generic options for GLP-1s?

Currently, there are no generic options for GLP-1s. If your insurance does not cover a GLP medication, your Care Team will help you identify other affordable options.

What are the most common side effects of GLP-1 medications?

The most common side effects are nausea, constipation, or other gastrointestinal discomfort. Your Care Team will advise you on the best ways to minimize side effects. Learn more about [the side effects of weight-loss medications](https://www.weightwatchers.com/us/blog/weight-loss/side-effects-weight-loss-medications).

Do you need to have diabetes to take GLP-1s?

No. Saxenda (liraglutide), Wegovy (semaglutide), and Zepbound (tirzepatide) are GLP-1 medications that are FDA approved specifically for the treatment of obesity.

How long can you stay on a GLP-1 medication?

GLP-1s are indicated for long-term use, much like other medications to treat chronic conditions. The effects stop immediately if you stop taking the medication, and it is likely in most cases that some weight regain will occur. As you reach your healthy goal weight, you should discuss with your clinician about adjusting your maintenance dose if necessary.
